angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 848,754 km at 252.69 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.9574 +/- 0.0247 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 252.69 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.22 +/- 0.15 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-26 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 848,754 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.86 +/- 0.34 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-26 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6034 +/- 31 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-26 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-26 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-26.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.200, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-26 (pscomppars): spectral type G0, from Smalley et al. 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010A&A...520A..56S/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WASP-26: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-26 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.16 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-26 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.28725, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-26 (pscomppars): age 6 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-26 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.2 km/s, from Albrecht et al. 2012 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012ApJ...757...18A/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
